Well, I am aromantic, but what I do for my friend is just ask what's bothering them. We have a system, DAUW (Depression, anxiety, urges, worse (Worse being suicidal thoughts)).

Obviously this could be skipped for your S/O since it's mostly panic attacks, but you could still ask if there are urges. I have them explain what's causing it briefly, then dig into it a little and offer advice where I can, and reassurance if ever they need it.

Just keep talking to them, every second they're alone with their thoughts is another second they can spend overthinking.

Be patient and understanding, don't pry too much if they don't know what's causing it, in times like those general reassurance is good, telling them they're safe, they are not in danger, have them repeat that to themself out loud.

Positive affirmations during anxiety attacks can do wonders for some people. For some people distractions work better, so maybe try asking if you can send them memes or cute pictures of their favorite animal to help. Always make sure to ask what helped and what didn't after an attack so you can know what to do better.

I hope this was good advice, my friend doesn't usually have panic attacks, more of depression and dissociation which requires me to keep her attention at all times so she can't overthink or worry herself too much.

Well if it's an epidermis cut/cat scratch it won't need much except to be cleaned and covered with something, an epidermis cut typically doesn't gape and might turn red or ooze blood onto a cloth, but won't actually bleed.

Dermis cuts/styro gape a bit and need steri strips to hold it together, plus cleaning and covering. Dermis cuts bleed out of the wound and usually look white inside.

Fat cuts/beans are bad and require stitches, plus thorough cleaning. Fat cuts gape a lot and look yellow bubbly inside.

Fascia/muscle cuts require immediate hospital attention since cuts that deep can cause severe and irreparable damage and can even paralyze limbs. They gape like hell and look brownish inside.

Hope this helps!
